one_line: Governments restrict AI tools, OpenAI expands services, compute capacity grows, and AI fuels drug research funding.

themes.title: Governments tighten AI use rules
themes.text: Swedish government ministries have prohibited staff from using ChatGPT and Claude on work computers, requiring Microsoft Copilot as the only approved AI tool. India will issue a consultation paper on AI legislation in the coming weeks, while major U.S. banks are restricting third‑party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, and Poland’s prime minister called for deeper AI, digital and space cooperation with India.

stories.headline: Swedish government offices ban ChatGPT and Claude, require Microsoft Copilot
India to issue AI law consultation paper in coming weeks, says minister
Major US banks block third‑party AI agents from customer accounts
Polish prime minister calls for deeper AI, digital and space cooperation with India

themes.title: OpenAI rolls out new tools
themes.text: OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available, adding voice and visual inputs and charging $0.10 per million input tokens. The company resumed training its most advanced models in an offline environment, added new offline and high‑compute red‑team containment measures, and terminated three safety researchers over alleged leaks of internal model designs. OpenAI also upgraded its Habitat storage system to support over one billion ChatGPT users, delivering reads twelve times faster.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens
OpenAI trains frontier AI models without internet access
OpenAI details new containment measures for frontier model training
OpenAI fires three safety researchers over alleged leak of internal model designs
OpenAI scales Habitat storage to deliver 12× faster reads for ChatGPT

themes.title: AI compute capacity expands worldwide
themes.text: SpaceX plans to manage at least 13 GW of AI compute power by the end of 2027, adding about 10 GW beyond earlier estimates. In Kazakhstan, Firebird obtained a U.S. export license for 45,000 NVIDIA Grace GPUs and is building a data center slated for commercial launch in Q3 2027, aiming for up to 500 MW of AI capacity.

stories.headline: SpaceX aims for 13 GW AI compute capacity by end of 2027
Kazakhstan expands AI compute with 45,000 Grace GPUs and new data centers

themes.title: AI accelerates drug research funding
themes.text: Warp Sciences raised $215 million to build AI‑powered chemistry contract labs focused on lead optimisation for biotech and pharma clients. Pathos AI announced a $237 million Series E round valuing it at $3 billion and a multi‑year collaboration with Bristol Myers Squibb and Tempus AI to apply its Foundry platform to Alzheimer’s and other neurological drug research.

Pathos AI raises $237 million Series E led by Bristol Myers Squibb
